Oliver —

Appreciate the clarity. I pulled together the quick pricing bands and the compact/full tradeoffs. See bullets below (short summary to keep this email digestible):

Compact (Metered)
- Billing: per-token and per-embedding usage.
- Good for: variable workloads, low initial commit.
- Downgrade path: N/A (no reserved capacity), you keep same feature set but no guaranteed throughput.
- Typical range for your 50 qps baseline: $6k–$9k/mo estimated (depends on model selection & caching).

Full (Reserved Dedicated)
- Billing: monthly reserved capacity with commit tiers + lower per-token overage.
- Good for: predictable throughput and costs, SLA-backed latency.
- Downgrade policy: we support step-down re-negotiations at quarter boundaries; partial proration for unused committed capacity on approved change requests.
- Typical range for 50–150 qps pilot: $28k–$45k/mo depending on GPU class and quantization profile.

Discounts/credits
- For a 12-month pilot committing to a modest reserved tier we can offer:
  - 10% standard pilot discount + one-time onboarding credit ($10k)
  - If Medlytics commits to 24 months, we can explore a 15% discount + waived setup fee.

Files attached: MAP-proposal-medlytics-20251106.pdf (draft MAP with milestone dates and acceptance criteria).

I’ll leave the fallback technical details to Naomi, but from a commercial perspective we’ll include explicit fallback SLA notes in the MAP and a clause for automatic model-variant fallback that reduces throughput guarantees but preserves availability.

Questions for Oliver:
- Do you want pricing in USD list price, or do you prefer a fully-burdened TCO-style quote your procurement can run?
- Confirm pilot start target (Jordan suggested week of Nov 24) and whether US-only regions are required.

Hi all —

Quick technical notes to complement Ben's pricing:

Fallback playbook (high level)
- Normal path: requests route to reserved pool (if chosen). KV/prefix caching reduces per-token cost and keeps latency stable.
- Degradation path: when capacity constrained we automatically route to a compatible model variant (smaller quantized model) with these properties:
  - Expected latency delta: +30–70ms median, 95th percentile increase depends on sustained QPS.
  - Throughput trade: variant reduces max sustained qps by ~30–50% but maintains functional outputs.
- Regional failover: if US region is saturated, we can burst to EU region (adds ~80–120ms median RTT). We recommend opt-in for cross-region burst for production-critical flows.

Downgrade & feature bundling implications
- For compact -> full: features are identical; full adds throughput guarantees, longer log retention, and dedicated tracing hooks.
- For full -> compact (downgrade): we capture a plan in the MAP with a checklist:
  - 30-day notice window, data export snapshot (audit logs/kv cache state), and a negotiated proration schedule.

Deliverables we will add to the MAP (Jordan/Ben):
- One-page fallback runbook (operational steps + decision tree).
- Short decision log template so Medlytics can record when fallback triggers and which model variant was used.

I attached a mutual action plan template I recommend we start filling out. If the pilot starts Nov 24, timeline looks like:
- Nov 10: MAP finalization + SOW sign-off
- Nov 17: Sandbox access + onboarding session
- Nov 24: Pilot go-live
